rationale: The Court is most likely to affirm on a narrow, text-focused reading of Rule 704(b): it bars only expert opinions about whether this defendant had the requisite mental state, leaving generalized modus-operandi testimony to be policed primarily by Rules 702/403 and limiting instructions. A Sotomayor dissent (possibly with Jackson) is likely to argue that in a courier case the testimony is a functional mens rea opinion that risks presumption-like effects inconsistent with 704(b)’s purpose and due-process concerns.
